title: Four fixed-rate stores can hide a routing change in one annual flow cycle and still give faster dry-event decline
abstract: We test whether a constant seasonal flow fraction and faster dry-event decline require faster store drainage. For parallel linear stores with equal recharge, equal mean and complex transfer at M frequencies force uniform routing when there are at most 2M+1 distinct rates. More rates leave an unmeasured routing subspace. Monotone selection cannot be exactly hidden. A positive four-store example retains 78.4% of flow throughout a steady annual sinusoidal cycle while its day-3 to day-8 decline index rises from 0.2079 to 0.2316. The rates stay fixed. A separate 70-digit calculation verifies the example. A linear feasibility tool, proofs, synthetic results and a water-balance check are included. The example uses scalar anchors from different Australian summaries; it is not a field fit. It does not explain the wet-year excess loss or identify the regional cause. Exact seasonal cancellation assumes equal recharge and a finite forcing spectrum.

display.caption: Synthetic four-store models share the same annual flow fraction but have different dry-event shapes. Additional frequencies expose the selected routing change.
